description.value: The Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale assessed emotion-regulation difficulties, including subscales such as lack of emotional awareness and lack of emotional clarity. It was administered before training and during training, with a post-training follow-up.

spans.text: To obtain a baseline score, patients were assessed with the DERS three times before the first training session, starting 1 week before the first session and followed by two further assessments with an interval of 2–3 days.
With the DERS, emotion regulation can be assessed in a comprehensive multi-factorized framework in adult populations ( Gratz and Roemer, 2004 ).
At the end of each run, a computerized version of the Dissociation Tension Scale-Short Version (DSS-4, ( Stiglmayr et al ., 2009 ), was presented.

description.value: The Dissociation Tension Scale-Short Version comprised four items assessing dissociative experiences on a 0–9 scale and one item assessing aversive tension. It was administered at the end of each run to measure dissociation and tension during training.

spans.text: The DSS-4 comprises four items assessing the degree of dissociative experiences on a 10-level scale (0 = not at all, 9 = very much) and one item on aversive tension.

clinical_characteristics.value: Ten female patients with BPD were recruited; two dropped out before the third session, leaving eight for final analyses. Mean age was 33.6 ± 9.5 years. Participants were in a 12-week inpatient Dialectical Behavior Therapy program, recruited no earlier than its fourth week, and were abstinent from alcohol and drugs for more than 2 months.

the standard preprocessing routine included slice time correction, realignment, unwarping, coregistration of the functional mean image to anatomy and normalization to the Montreal Neurological Institute standard template and smoothing
smoothing (full width at half maximum = 8 mm)

description.value: Functional images were preprocessed in SPM8 by discarding the first 10 volumes, slice-time correction, realignment, unwarping, coregistration of the functional mean image to the anatomical image, normalization to the Montreal Neurological Institute template, and spatial smoothing with an 8 mm FWHM kernel. Motion and global-intensity outlier volumes were detected with ART and censored; realignment and nuisance regressors were included in the models.

spans.text: BPD patients participated in four rtfMRI NF training sessions

description.value: Participants viewed aversive or scrambled pictures and attempted to down-regulate amygdala activity using thermometer feedback across four sessions.

spans.text: each condition was presented five times per run in semi-randomized order
‘regulate’

description.value: Participants viewed an aversive picture and were instructed to down-regulate the thermometer feedback display representing their amygdala BOLD signal.

spans.text: In the ‘regulate’ condition, participants were instructed to down-regulate a thermometer displayed at both sides of an aversive picture presented on a computer monitor.
‘view’

description.value: Participants viewed an aversive picture and received the same type of feedback, but were instructed to respond naturally to the picture content without attempting to regulate it.

spans.text: In the ‘view’ condition, an aversive picture was also displayed together with feedback, but participants were instructed to respond naturally to the picture content.
‘neutral’

description.value: Participants viewed scrambled pictures while receiving feedback for comparable visual stimulation; this was a control condition without aversive emotional content.

spans.text: In the ‘neutral’ condition, scrambled pictures were presented.

presentation_software.value: Not specified; feedback was presented using TurboBrainVoyager 3.0.

instructions.value: In the regulate condition, participants were instructed to down-regulate the thermometer display while viewing an aversive picture. In the view condition, they were instructed to respond naturally to the picture content. In the neutral condition, they viewed scrambled pictures. During resting-state scans they were instructed to keep their eyes open.

stimuli.value: Aversive pictures depicting scenes from war and accidents and people and animals suffering; scrambled pictures in the neutral condition; and a thermometer display showing the amygdala BOLD signal.

spans.text: One hundred pictures were obtained from published sets ( Lang et al ., 2008 ; Wessa et al ., 2010 ) and complemented by 40 pictures from the internet, depicting scenes from war and accidents and also scenes of people and animals suffering.

value: Amygdala BOLD signal used as neurofeedback
